financing.summary: Adams Homes is a private, family-controlled builder with no SEC filings, no public notes and no ratings, so almost nothing about its balance sheet is disclosed. What the public record does show is a two-company model: the affiliated Pensacola lot developer Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC buys and develops land and sells finished lots to Adams Homes in blocks (two 50-lot takedowns at $4.25M each were recorded in Jacksonville in June and October 2026), so Garden Street already does the job a land banker would do, inside the family. A county-records aggregator shows the money behind it is bank debt: Texas Capital Bank, Regions Bank, Synovus Bank and Wells Fargo Bank are the largest mortgagees of record on Adams Homes entities, and Centennial Bank recorded a $100.0M mortgage on Garden Street on 2026-05-05. No land banker, lot-option fund or joint-venture partner is publicly linked to either company, which means the opening for Domain is to supplement or replace bank-funded land held by Garden Street, and the people to reach are Bryan (William B.) Adams and the Garden Street land team.
financing.land_strategy: Not stated by the company; no owned/optioned target is published. In practice it is a captive-developer model: Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC (founded 2016, same Pensacola building) acquires and develops land in about twenty Southeastern markets and sells finished lots to homebuilders, and recorded deeds show Adams Homes of Northwest Florida, Inc. buying those lots in 50-lot blocks. Adams Homes also buys single scattered lots directly in older platted Florida communities and runs a build-on-your-lot program in a few Florida divisions.

lots.source_title: Elementix company profile: Adams Homes (aggregated recorded-document data, 'as of November 2026')
lots.note: Not publicly disclosed (private company, no filings). The only quantitative hint is a third-party public-records aggregator showing about 2,046 current property ownerships across 34 Adams-linked entities (1,211 of them in Adams Homes of Northwest Florida, Inc. and 31 in Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC). That is a count of recorded parcels (lots plus homes under construction, and for Garden Street large undivided tracts), not a controlled-lot figure, and it says nothing about lots under contract or option.

land_banking.description: Privately held residential lot developer founded in 2016 and headquartered at 100 W Garden St, Pensacola (Adams Homes is in the same building). It buys land, entitles and develops it, and sells finished single-family and townhome lots to homebuilders, aimed at entry-level, first move-up and active-adult product. It says it works in three regions and twenty markets across FL, GA, AL, NC, SC and TX; its locations page also lists Mississippi.
land_banking.note: Verified here is Garden Street's own description of its business. Its site does not name Adams Homes or state who owns it; the link to Adams Homes is documented in the next rows. Garden Street's job postings (Nov 2026) call it one of the largest privately held residential land developers in the Southeast, operating in seven states.

land_banking.description: Adams Homes treats Garden Street staff as its own people: its 2025 Founder's Club awards (company blog, July 2026) include a Director of Land Development in Spring Hill credited for his work on 'the Garden Street team' and on significant deals. Land acquisition and lot development for Adams Homes therefore sit inside Garden Street.
land_banking.source_title: Adams Homes blog: 2025 Founder's Club Trip (2026-07-28)
land_banking.note: The company does not publish the legal ownership of Garden Street. Texas Comptroller records put Adams Homes Lone Star, LLC at 100 W Garden St, Floor 4, with William B. Adams as the only listed managing member (2026 report); Garden Street's site gives Floor 3 of the same address.

land_banking.description: County-record signatures tie the two companies to the same people: the aggregator shows William Adams as officer/member on 18 affiliated entities including Adams Homes of Northwest Florida, Inc. and Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC (FL and AL), and lists Garden Street among the 34 entities in the Adams Homes group.
land_banking.note: Third-party aggregator that reads signatures on recorded documents with AI; it shows common signers, not ownership percentages, and it contains some noise (one person page also attaches an unrelated national builder). Treat as strong evidence of common control, not as proof of legal ownership.

land_banking.description: Lot takedown: Adams Homes of Northwest Florida Inc. bought 50 residential lots in Baldwin Point (Old Plank Road, Jacksonville, Duval County) from Garden Street Communities Southeast LLC for $4,250,000, about $85,000 a lot. Deed recorded June 1-7, 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Jacksonville Daily Record: Top commercial sales of the week (2026-06-11)
land_banking.note: Per-lot price is my arithmetic from the reported total.

land_banking.description: Second takedown in the same community: Adams Homes of Northwest Florida Inc. bought another 50 residential lots in Baldwin Point (location given as Whitehouse Air Field, Jacksonville) from Garden Street Communities Southeast LLC for $4,250,000. Deed recorded September 28 to October 4, 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Jacksonville Daily Record: Top commercial sales of the week (2026-10-08)
land_banking.note: Same lot count and price about four months after the first, which points to a scheduled block-takedown agreement between the affiliates rather than one-off sales. The paper lists this as a separate recording in a different week with a different street reference, so it is entered as a second transaction; the takedown contract itself is not public.

debt.instrument: Secured bank borrowings recorded as mortgages on Adams Homes entities (facility terms not disclosed)
debt.lenders_agent: Texas Capital Bank; Regions Bank; Synovus Bank; Wells Fargo Bank (largest mortgagees of record per aggregator; agent bank and current lender group not confirmed)
debt.source_title: Elementix company profile: Adams Homes (aggregated recorded-document data, 'as of November 2026')
debt.note: The company page ranks lenders by recorded mortgage volume: Texas Capital Bank (117 loans), Regions Bank (85 loans), Wells Fargo Bank (90 loans). The pages for the people who sign the mortgages (William Adams; Don Adams, shown as Vice President; Matthew Shook, shown as General Counsel) rank Texas Capital Bank, Synovus Bank and Regions Bank for 2015 to 2026. The dollar totals are face amounts of mortgages recorded county by county, so one facility is counted many times (the page shows $12.9B in one place and $3.5B in another); they are not balances and are not used here. The pattern (the same few banks on hundreds of county recordings) is what a syndicated, mortgage-secured borrowing-base facility looks like, but that structure is my inference. Tagged Inferred because size, maturity, agent and whether each bank is still in the group are not public; on the general counsel's page the latest mortgage he signed dates from 2023.

debt.instrument: Centennial Bank mortgage loan to Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC ($100.0M face amount, recorded 2026-05-05)
debt.source_title: Elementix investor profile: Bryan Adams (aggregated recorded-document data, 'as of November 2026')
debt.note: Borrower is the affiliated lot developer, not Adams Homes. The aggregator shows two $100.0M Centennial Bank mortgages on Garden Street dated 05/05/2026, both marked Open; identical date and amount suggest one facility recorded in more than one county. $100.0M is the recorded face amount (the maximum secured), not the drawn balance. Across all of Bryan Adams' entities (not Garden Street alone) the page shows Centennial Bank as the top lender (10 loans, $395.0M) and BankPlus second (1 loan, $7.7M); the Garden Street entity itself shows 7 recorded mortgages with no lender breakdown. Rate, maturity, guarantors and whether Adams Homes guarantees it are not public. Light check 2026-11-19: corrected the earlier note, which called Centennial Garden Street's dominant lender with 10 loans; those counts are Bryan Adams-level totals.

capital_events.description: Centennial Bank recorded a $100.0M mortgage against Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC, the affiliated lot developer that supplies Adams Homes (shown twice on the same date, status Open).
capital_events.source_title: Elementix investor profile: William Adams (aggregated recorded-document data, 'as of November 2026')
capital_events.note: Face amount of the recorded mortgage, not a drawn balance; could be a new facility or a renewal or upsize of an existing Centennial line (the aggregator counts 10 Centennial loans on Garden Street in all). Underlying county record not opened.

key_metrics.source_title: SEC EDGAR company search for 'adams homes' (no matching companies)

gaps: Owned vs optioned lots, total lots controlled, years of supply: not publicly disclosed (private company, no filings). Garden Street's lot inventory and pipeline: not publicly disclosed.

Land-banking or lot-option financing partner: none publicly identified. No public link found to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon, Varde (site search: no results), Walton Global (site search: no relevant results), Forestar, Essential Housing, IHP Capital, DW Partners, Brookfield, Oaktree, GTIS or Hearthstone. The affiliated developer Garden Street Communities fills that role.

Legal ownership of Garden Street Communities Southeast, LLC and its exact relationship to Adams Homes (common owner, subsidiary, or separate family entity): not stated in any source opened. Florida Sunbiz officer records returned a bot check and were not opened.

Terms between Adams Homes and Garden Street (option deposits, takedown schedules, pricing, whether lots are also sold to other builders): not publicly disclosed. Only two recorded takedowns (Jacksonville, 2026) were found.

Adams Homes credit facility: size, structure, maturity, agent bank, covenants and current lender group not publicly disclosed. Texas Capital Bank, Regions Bank, Synovus Bank and Wells Fargo Bank appear only through a county-records aggregator; none is confirmed as a current lender by a primary source.

Garden Street's Centennial Bank loan: rate, maturity, guarantors and drawn balance not publicly disclosed; the $100.0M figure is the recorded face amount from an aggregator, and the county record itself was not opened.
Senior notes, term loans, private placements: none found. EDGAR company search returns no registrant named Adams Homes, so there is no SEC-registered or 144A reporting trail.
Credit ratings: none found (no rated public debt identified).
Cash, total debt, liquidity, net debt to capital, fiscal year end: not publicly disclosed.
Joint ventures and outside equity or capital partners: none publicly reported.

Ownership and succession: the company calls Wayne Adams its late founder and his son Bryan (William B.) Adams is the only officer on the Texas entity records; the split of ownership within the Adams family, any estate or trust arrangements, and any sale process are not publicly disclosed.

M&A in 2025 and 2026: none found in the sources opened (company blog and site, local press searches). The swarm's shared web-search allowance was used up before this run started, so trade press was not swept by search; absence of a deal is not confirmed.
Florida CDD bond offering documents for Garden Street communities (which would describe developer financing and builder lot contracts) were not searched.
